entries.note: This appears within Marcus’s summary of Saunders’s key points; attribution to Marcus alone is uncertain. It asserts a possibility, not a firm predicted release.
Presented as Saunders’s point, but explicitly endorsed by Marcus through his reference to his own Senate testimony.

entries.test: US laws in force on August 23, 2024 would show whether external advisory bodies had a legally required strong role in weighing risks and benefits of major AI company decisions.
entries.note: The proposition broadens the absence of the specified advisory role into an absence of any external governance.
Calling this concentration of power terrifying expresses an evaluative judgment.

entries.test: Public records would establish whether the referenced board existed by publication and whether any subsequently established board obtained substantive authority without a government mandate.
entries.note: The supplied text does not establish that Altman promised a public board. The record combines a historical assertion with an undated conditional forecast.

entries.test: Comparisons of SB-1047’s earlier and August 23, 2024 versions would show whether amendments reduced its obligations, oversight, or enforcement powers.
entries.note: The description of the bill as a small step is evaluative, but the claimed weakening has a plain legislative test.
“Meagre” evaluates the adequacy of OpenAI’s reasons.

entries.test: Dated OpenAI submissions, public correspondence, and legislative records would show whether OpenAI proposed SB-1047 amendments months before its August 2024 opposition.
entries.note: Marcus’s closing sentence adopts the preceding allegation. The good-faith framing is evaluative; the absence of earlier proposals is checkable.

entries.test: Public records of AI companies’ safety commitments, compliance, and voluntary enforcement would show whether self-regulation can deliver sustained adherence without external accountability.
entries.note: The sentence links predicted failure to a lack of accountability. Its categorical “never” can be challenged by a demonstrated successful case.

entries.test: The public record of SB-1047’s defeat and subsequent state and federal AI requirements would show whether governance remained substantially dependent on voluntary company rules.
entries.note: The proposition drops the stated condition that OpenAI and others succeed in defeating the bill. SB-1047 was vetoed in 2024, so evidence about the aftermath is available.
“Unaccountable” strengthens “almost no accountability.” Humanity’s fate being determined by a few leaders, with unspecified bad results, lacks a shared decisive test.
Marcus rejects the plausibility assessment; he does not categorically predict that AGI will fail to arrive in that period.
“Could” expresses a possible consequence rather than a firm conditional prediction.
